overview: AutoBuild queues fixed decorative block patterns (Penis, Surround, Singular) through C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement, firing them straight into the NetHandler's no-event queue so they skip the module event bus entirely. Normal mode builds at the player's feet on a configurable tick interval; Teleport mode waits for the use-item key, ray-traces to a looked-at block, computes a path with MainPathFinder on a separate thread, streams C04PacketPlayerPosition hops along it, builds at the target, then walks the path back in reverse. A blanket onPacketSend handler cancels every C08 that reaches the event bus, so the only placements the server ever sees are the module's own direct-queue packets.

sections.p: The module also owns an onPacketSend handler that cancels every C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement arriving on the event bus. Because build() uses PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent, which calls addToSendQueueWithoutEvent and bypasses the bus, its own placements are untouched; the cancel only suppresses placements from vanilla right-clicks or other modules while AutoBuild is active.

Teleport mode bypasses the tick gate: the outer condition fires whenever the mode is not Normal or Auto Disable is on, so the mode is driven purely by the key and the 100ms timer rather than the tick counter.

sections.h: Placement patterns and the direct queue
sections.p: All C08s go through sendPacketWithoutEvent, so they bypass onPacketSend's own cancel and reach the server as an unswung, same-tick burst of placements: one invocation emits between one and five C08s with no C0A animations in between.

files.label: AutoBuild.java
files.explanation: The whole module is one class. onUpdate drives the tick gate and dispatches Normal vs Teleport mode; onPacketSend cancels every C08 that reaches the event bus; build() is the placement engine that fires between one and five C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement packets per invocation through the no-event queue, with an optional C09PacketHeldItemChange switch-around when Next Slot is on. The Swing setting declared at the top is never read, so the module never sends C0A arm-swing packets. Teleport mode hands the pathfinding to MainPathFinder on a new Thread and streams the out-and-back journey as C04PacketPlayerPosition hops.

files.label: MainPathFinder.java (teleport pathfinder)
files.explanation: A block-grid A*-style pathfinder over four horizontal directions (the directions array holds +X, -X, +Z, -Z), with a start and end Vec3 floored to block coordinates and an open PathHub list expanded via compute(). Teleport mode calls MainPathFinder.computePath(start, end) on a worker thread, then converts every Vec3 in the returned path into a C04PacketPlayerPosition with onGround true, streams it through the no-event queue to reach the build site, and reverses the path to come back.

countering.label: FastPlace (placement rate)
countering.explanation: NCP's FastPlace check scores every placement into data.fastPlaceBuckets (a frequency bucket accumulator keyed by wall-clock time) and maintains a short-term window: fastPlaceShortTermCount increments for every placement landing within cc.fastPlaceShortTermTicks of the first, resetting when the window elapses or server lag exceeds the adaption threshold. AutoBuild emits one to five C08s per invocation and, at the default Tick=1, repeats that burst every single tick - a placement rate no hand can produce, so both the full-period bucket score and the short-term count grow on the first burst. The check's cancellation actions (cc.fastPlaceActions) then eat subsequent placements outright.

countering.label: NoSwing (arm movement between places)
countering.explanation: NoSwing requires an arm swing (C0A) between consecutive placements: each placement without a preceding swing increments data.noSwingCount, and once it exceeds 1 the violation level grows by 1 and the configured actions run. AutoBuild never sends C0A packets at all - the Swing setting is declared but never referenced, and build() queues only C08s - so every multi-block invocation is a chain of swingless placements. The Penis pattern's middle-plus-balls-plus-height sequence (up to five C08s in one tick) is exactly the burst NoSwing was written for: no human can place five blocks without ever moving their arm.

countering.label: Direction (placement outside field of view)
countering.explanation: The Direction check (an AbstractBlockDirectionCheck) computes the angular distance between the player's look vector and the block being interacted with, adding the distance to directionVL and firing the configured actions once the accumulated score crosses the threshold. AutoBuild places at fixed offsets - two blocks east/south of the player in Normal Penis mode, above the player's feet for the height loop, and on all four horizontal faces in Surround mode - while the player's view stays wherever it was when the burst fired. Those side and above placements sit outside the field of view, which is precisely the interaction pattern Direction is built to flag.

countering.label: BlockInteractSpeed (same-tick placements)
countering.explanation: Hawk's BlockInteractSpeed records the server tick of every block interaction per player and punishes any second interaction landing in the same tick (pp.getCurrentTick() == lastPlaceTick), rewarding otherwise. AutoBuild's build() emits between one and five C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement packets in a single invocation, all processed in the same tick, so every multi-block pattern trips the same-tick comparison immediately. Even the single-block Singular mode fails when Tick=1 because consecutive invocations arrive one tick apart - the minimum human cadence for block placement is several ticks per block.
